summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of sclerosing mesenteritis, gastroparesis, and G-tube dependence was admitted for failure to thrive, persistent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain following discontinuation of home TPN due to insurance issues. She had lost 32 pounds and presented with malnutrition and hypocalcemia. During the 12-day admission, her G-tube was initially replaced to improve venting, but due to ongoing low output, it was subsequently changed to a Wills-Ogelsby tube, which improved drainage. A tunneled femoral central line was placed to reinitiate TPN after insurance approval. Nausea was managed with octreotide, ondansetron, and ativan, while dronabinol was discontinued due to sedation. Chronic pain remained stable on home medications. She was monitored for infection with negative blood and stool cultures. Upon discharge, she was stable on nightly TPN, with plans for weekly chem-10 monitoring, visiting nurse support, and follow-up with her care team.
